summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization: QPS, concurrency, token distributions, latency SLOs and benchmark plan. Customer is evaluating Redwood for an embedding+chat use case across transactional flows and fraud analyst workflows. Agreed data deliverables and initial timeline for hosted baseline next week.
topics: Traffic modeling: QPS and peak concurrency
Input/output token distribution and typical prompt templates
Hosted vs Dedicated sizing and rough cost tradeoffs
Benchmark plan and artifacts to collect
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Jordan from Redwood, AE. Quick introductions?
[00:06] Samir: Samir Patel, Head of ML at Monetix.
[00:09] Alyssa: Alyssa Chen, platform eng.
[00:11] Marcus: Marcus Reed, CTO.
[00:13] Priya: Priya Nadar, SE, I’ll lead the sizing/benchmarks.
[00:17] Jordan: Great. Goal today is to scope a POC for workload characterization — we want QPS, concurrency, token distributions, latency targets, and a plan for benchmarks. We sent a short questionnaire, did you all see?
[00:27] Nina: Yep saw it, filled some sections but Samir will add the traffic traces.
[00:31] Samir: Yeah I can share traces, but need to anonymize; we can do last 7 days.
[00:36] Priya: Perfect. High-level: can you describe the Monetix flows you want to run through the model? Chat? Embeddings? Rerank?
[00:44] Samir: Two primary flows. First is a customer support chat where we do retrieval-augmented generation — short prompts, often 30-80 input tokens, outputs 40-150 tokens. Throughput peaks around business hours, average QPS per endpoint ~12, peak burst to 120 QPS for ~10 mins during incidents. Second is an internal fraud-analyst assistant that runs longer prompts including transaction history, avg input tokens ~350-700 and outputs ~200-400, much lower QPS — single digits but concurrency high when analyst batch runs (around 20 concurrent sessions).
[01:20] Priya: Good, that gives us two very different profiles. For the chat path, are you doing streaming to the client?
[01:25] Alyssa: Yes streaming to the web client, and we care a lot about end-to-end latency under load.
[01:30] Jordan: What's your target SLO? 95th percentile? 99th?
[01:34] Marcus: For customer-facing chat, 95th < 300ms generation time would be ideal but we might accept up to 500ms if accuracy is better. For analyst tools 95th < 1s is acceptable.
[01:46] Priya: Noted. Also helpful: do you have token histograms per endpoint? Average and 95th for input/output?
[01:53] Samir: We can produce those, we'll export as CSV. Typical chat input mean ~60, p95 ~140; output mean ~90, p95 ~220. Fraud assistant mean input ~480, p95 ~950, output mean ~300.
[02:07] Priya: Great. That maps to memory/KV cache sizing too. For long inputs we need to know kv cache usage across requests.
[02:14] Jordan: On deployment mode, initial POC — do you want hosted Redwood API, or Dedicated/private?
[02:20] Marcus: Start hosted to move fast. If numbers look good we want Dedicated or Private (VPC) later for data residency.
[02:26] Jordan: Cool, we can baseline hosted then produce Dedicated sizing recommendation. Any regulatory constraints?
[02:30] Marcus: PCI-adjacent, but mostly need audit logs, encryption at rest, and KMS integration eventually. SOC2 is required.
[02:37] Priya: We have SOC2 and can do KMS/HSM for Private. For the POC hosted baseline we'll share anonymized logs and provide a temporary test tenant.
[02:46] Alyssa: About cost — do you have rough cost guidance for high QPS vs dedicated? Our current infra team is sensitive to token cost per million.
[02:54] Jordan: We will include rough cost modeling based on your sample traffic. Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated has committed capacity which lowers per-token cost at scale. We'll include ballpark in the POC runbook.
[03:03] Priya: Back to workload modeling — what QPS distribution do you see throughout the day? Is 12 QPS average steady or spiky?
[03:10] Samir: 12 QPS average for the chat endpoint over global business hours (about 14 hours), overnight drops to 2-3 QPS. Spikes 2-3x baseline during marketing sends; rare but do happen.
[03:20] Priya: For benchmarking we typically run: steady-state QPS at your 75th percentile, then burst tests at 2x and 5x for short windows, and long-run throughput to look for tail latency/jitter.
[03:31] Samir: Sounds good. For the fraud assistant, concurrency is more important: 20 concurrent sessions each with long sequences.
[03:38] Priya: Right — long-context runs exercise KV cache and memory. We'll want to test cold-start latency for sessions and then sustained sequence generation.
[03:45] Jordan: One thing to call out — quantization options can change latency and memory characteristics. For very long contexts, 8-bit quant might help memory but could add slight quality/regression risk. We can try a couple of model variants.
[03:57] Samir: Are you supporting LLaMA-family and other open models?
[04:00] Priya: Yes, we curate a model catalog. But note — transcription: sometimes names get mixed up, like 'Llama' becomes 'lama' in notes, so forgive that. We'll propose 2 model variants: a faster quantized 13B and a higher-quality 33B for comparison.
[04:16] Alyssa: For the POC we want to see both latency and a small quality eval set — maybe 200 prompts for each flow with human labels.
[04:25] Samir: We'll provide the eval set for chat and the fraud assistant metrics (precision on flag suggestions).
[04:30] Priya: Good. Benchmarks we'll capture: median, p95, p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory pressure, and cost per 1M tokens extrapolated. Also error rates and tail jitter.
[04:41] Marcus: For the streaming chat, do you measure time-to-first-byte and full response time separately?
[04:45] Priya: Yes, we capture TTFB (time-to-first-token) and end-to-end completion. Streaming tends to hide higher late-token latency but TTFB is critical for UX.
[04:54] Jordan: Can you confirm concurrency model for your client? Is each browser tab a persistent session or do you open new connections per request?
[04:59] Alyssa: Persistent websockets, so connection count is roughly number of active users. We estimate 1.2x connections per QPS because users often have background pings.
[05:08] Priya: Ok we'll simulate websockets with persistent connections during the benchmark.
[05:12] Samir: Security Q: for hosted POC can we limit data retention and ensure logs are scoped to tenant?
[05:18] Jordan: Yes, we can configure retention for POC and show audit logs. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
[05:23] Alyssa: For the private option later — do you support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS?
[05:29] Priya: Yes for Redwood Private we can do VPC with peering or PrivateLink and customer KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include details in the runbook.
[05:36] Marcus: Timeline wise we want results in 2 weeks — is that realistic?
[05:40] Priya: For an initial baseline hosted run, yes: share traces by Mon/Tue, Redwood runs baseline mid-week, results and sizing by next Monday, follow-up sync then. Full dedicated sizing might take longer.
[05:50] Jordan: Let's lock dates: Jordan will send runbook by Friday (2026-07-10), Monetix will send traces and histograms by Monday (2026-07-13). Priya will run baseline during week of 2026-07-13 and share results 2026-07-17.
[06:05] Nina: Quick question — how do you handle fallback if capacity is constrained? We have strict uptime requirements.
[06:10] Priya: We have smart routing and fallbacks: route to a lower-cost variant or a smaller model for soft degradation. We can test failovers in the POC.
[06:18] Samir: Good. Also curious about batching impacts on latency for the chat flow — we want low latency so batching might not help.
[06:24] Diego: (joined in) Hi all, Diego from solutions eng. On batching: continuous batching helps throughput but we tune thresholds for latency-sensitive endpoints. For chat we'll likely keep batch sizes small and prioritize latency.
[06:36] Alyssa: Does Redwood expose per-token cost breakdown in the console?
[06:40] Jordan: Yes we show token-level cost, model-level breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. We'll include screenshots in the runbook.
[06:47] Priya: Back to modeling — please include the following in the traffic artifact: time-series of QPS, histograms for input and output token lengths, percent of streaming vs non-streaming, and sample prompts.
[06:58] Samir: We'll do that. We can also flag which flows require PII handling.
[07:03] Marcus: One more — we may want to compare to our in-house GPU fleet for cost/latency. Can you provide raw metric exports so we can run side-by-side analysis?
[07:11] Priya: Yes we'll provide raw CSVs with timestamps, latencies, gpu util. For hosted we provide the run VM metrics too.
[07:18] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps — I’ll send runbook, Priya will run baseline, Monetix provides traces/eval set, follow-up 2026-07-20 to review results.
[07:26] Nina: Thanks all.
[07:27] Samir: Thanks.
[07:29] Jordan: End of call.
